newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the South, rice prices were mostly steady. Long grain milled rice was selling mostly at $19.50 per cwt, medium grain traded mostly at $18.00 to $19.00, second heads were steady at $14.00 to $15.00 and brewers remain in very tight supply with few quotes at $14.50 to $15.25, but no confirmed sales were reported. Rice by-products were steady to $5.00 higher.
In California, rice prices were steady with medium grain selling mostly at $19.50. Rice bran was uneven, selling $5.00 lower to $4.00 higher.

California rice ship loadings for the week ended November 30 at the Port of Sacramento: the Aomori Willow loaded 9,000.44 tonnes of U.S. No 1 bagged medium grain milled rice and 1,000.18 tonnes of U.S. No 1 second heads for export to Japan. At the Port of Stockton, the CS Ocean loaded 10,000.62 tonnes of U.S. No 1 medium grain bagged brown rice destined for Japan.

Inspections of California rice for export: There were 441,148 cwt of U.S. medium grain milled rice inspected for the week ended November 30. The yearly total since October 1, 1996 is 1,207,594 cwt, compared to 1,294,460 cwt a year ago.

The following prices were for domestic shipment -- offers, FOB mills, milled rice, dollars per cwt, bagged. (All milled rice grade 2 not to exceed 4 percent brokens, except California grade 1. All second heads grade 4 or better)
Feed by-products prices (dollars per short ton, fob mills).
